narrative.overview: José Planeja renders household money with the calm authority of a premium metal card and a private-bank statement, never a playful budgeting toy. The world is monochromatic electric-blue (a single hue ~240 degrees): a live primary from pure #0000F3 through the working #2626EE/#4F4FFF and up into periwinkle tints. Every surface carries real depth (offset + soft blur shadows) and a 1px top highlight that reads like the milled edge of a metal card, the signature move of the system. Corners are crisp and tight; nothing is a pill. Two themes stand as equals, switched by [data-theme] with a prefers-color-scheme mirror. Light is a cool periwinkle-tinted near-white paper with deep navy ink; dark is deep-navy card grounds with periwinkle ink. The product is mobile-first (a Brazilian pt-BR / BRL PWA for families), so density, touch targets, and a left slide-in drawer hub drive the shell. The world refuses the soft/rounded/pastel budget-app default and the cream-serif or near-black-plus-neon AI-generic look. The one idea it owns: money rendered with the weight of a statement.
keyCharacteristics: Monochromatic electric-blue, one hue ~240 degrees, from pure blue through periwinkle.
The 1px metal-card-edge top highlight on every raised surface.
Crisp, tight corners (3-16px); never a pill except on data-bar tracks and status dots.
Tabular numerals on every money figure.
Two first-class themes: periwinkle paper / navy ink, and navy ground / periwinkle ink.
A left drawer hub as the navigation model, with an electric-blue active spine.

rules.name: The One Spine Rule
rules.body: Pure electric-blue emphasis marks one thing per view - the primary action and the active nav row. Its rarity is what makes the statement figure and the active spine read.

rules.name: The Semantic-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red appear only where they carry financial meaning (income, caution, expense/debt). They never decorate. Everything else is the blue field or a neutral.

rules.name: The Dual-Theme Parity Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are equals, not a primary plus an afterthought. Never hardcode a hex for a themed role; reference the CSS custom property so both themes and the system-preference mirror stay correct.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Any figure that represents money uses tabular numerals and tight negative tracking (down to -1.5px at statement size). Money is a column, not prose.

rules.name: The Metal-Edge Rule
rules.body: Every raised surface (card, panel, drawer, KPI, logo tile, button) carries the --edge top highlight together with its drop shadow. The pairing is the brand; a surface with a shadow but no edge, or an edge but no depth, is off-world.

dos: Do pair --edge with a drop shadow on every raised surface - the metal-card edge is the signature.
Do render every money figure with tabular numerals and tight negative tracking; keep money in columns.
Do reference themed roles through C.* / var(--*) so both themes and the system-preference mirror stay correct.
Do keep pure electric-blue emphasis rare - one primary action and one active nav row per view.
Do use crisp corners from the 3-16px scale; reserve 999px for bar tracks and status dots only.
donts: Don't ship pill-shaped or flat/shadowless buttons - corners are 5px and depth is real.
Don't use green/amber/red decoratively; they carry financial meaning only.
Don't hardcode a hex for a themed role, or build a light-only surface - the two themes are equals.
Don't introduce serif or cream/pastel budget-app or near-black + neon AI-generic treatments; this world is monochromatic electric-blue.
Don't canonize the legacy .tab-strip as a navigation pattern; the drawer hub is the model.
